thread:
incident-bot: Pager: high error rate and 95th percentile latency spike on inference cluster serving /v1/embeddings and /v1/rerank. Alert rule: infra.inference.error_rate > 5% for 3m. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.company/r/inf-prod

maya: I'm paged, taking lead. I'll gather quick scope. Can someone dump recent tail latencies and top routes?

sanjay: grabbing metrics now. Early look: embeddings QPS up 3x from baseline, top of heap memory pressure on nodes, KV cache thrash. Chat is healthy but rerank endpoints have rising 5xxs.

taylor: adding context — we rolled a lightweight embeddings model yesterday (v2-quant) and set relaxed per-route limits for a single partner; likely traffic storm + model mem spike.

lucy (support): Support reports Customer X and Customer Y reported timeouts ~10:32am — files attached in Zendesk 4321, 4322. They tried bulk-embedding batches.

maya: initial mitigation plan: 1) tighten per-endpoint global quotas for embeddings and rerank, 2) increase chat priority routing to preserve SLAs, 3) if needed, disable rerank for public tier for 15m. Anyone object?

sanjay: agree. Proposed numbers: reduce embeddings global QPS to 30% of normal and per-customer simultaneous batch limit to 2. Rerank: global QPS -> 0 (disable) for non-enterprise routes. Chat keep at 80%.

taylor: +1. Also recommend enabling traffic-shaping policy that routes partner A to dedicated pool (they allowed it) to reduce contention.

ops-bot: Executing quota change: POST /admin/quotas/modify  {"route":"/v1/embeddings","scope":"global","qps":0.3} (dry-run)

maya: ops-bot run actual change now. Use safe rollback TTL=20m.

ops-bot: Change applied: /v1/embeddings global qps set to 30% (effective), per-customer concurrent batches capped at 2. Rerank routes disabled for public tier. Chat route weight increased to 80% capacity.

sanjay: metrics update in 3m. Early signs: error rate for embeddings dropped to 1.2%, 95p latency back to baseline. Rerank 5xxs dropped to 0 after disable.

lucy (support): Heads up: telling impacted customers about temporary quota change. Draft message: "We're throttling large embedding requests temporarily to stabilize performance; we expect full service in ~20 minutes. Contact support for priority handling."

maya: good. Also we need to track who had requests dropped so we can credit usage. Add `ingest.traffic.drop_log` to incident timeline.

eric: small note — ensure billing won't auto-charge customers for partial failures; finance flagged one alert.

ops-bot: Created incident ticket INC-2026-2480003456, linked to runbook: https://docs.redwood.company/runbooks/traffic-mitigation

maya: prepping handoff in 10m to night oncall. @sanjay stay as day responder, @eric coordinate billing/support. tldr: embeddings throttled to 30%, rerank disabled for public tier, chat preserved.

sanjay: I'll keep monitoring. If embeddings QPS remains elevated but stable, we'll gradually relax to 50% in 10m increments. If memory pressure resumes, we force-evict model v2-quant from shared pool and revert to v1-embed.

taylor: FYI config to change per-route limits (for documentation):
```
# admin API example
POST /admin/quotas/modify HTTP/1.1
Host: admin.redwood.company
Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "route": "/v1/embeddings",
  "scope": "global",
  "limits": {
    "qps_ratio": 0.3,
    "concurrent_per_customer": 2,
    "ttl_minutes": 20
  }
}
```

maya: leaving note: when we re-enable rerank, do it behind canary flag and keep per-route throttle at 50% for 30m. Also schedule a post-incident action: enforce per-customer bulk-embedding thresholds and add preemptive circuit-breaker for new model rollouts.

lucy (support): customers notified. Ticketing: please add follow-up triage with product for model rollout checklist.

ops-bot: Next check-in scheduled in 10 minutes. Incident assigned to INC-2026-2480003456.

maya: handoff to night oncall @eric in 8m. Key state: embeddings throttled (30%), rerank disabled for public, chat normal. Ongoing: monitor memory, error rate, and dropped request logs.

eric: acknowledged. I'll take the 2nd shift and keep the throttle in place until stability confirmed or exec approval to relax.

maya: closing race — great response. Postmortem assigned to taylor + sanjay to analyze root cause (model mem behaviour + partner burst). Add quantization regression checks to Optimize pipeline. :white_check_mark:
